DO_NOT_STATE_AS_FACT: Do NOT state or imply the five were involved in the attack in any way. DNA identified Matias Reyes as the sole source; he said he acted alone; all convictions are vacated. They are the Exonerated Five.

ledger.claim: Episode identity and R2 dignity frame
ledger.detail: This is the story of five Black and Latino teenagers — Antron McCray, Kevin Richardson, Yusef Salaam, Raymond Santana, and Korey Wise — who were coerced into false confessions, wrongfully convicted in 1990 for the 1989 Central Park jogger attack, imprisoned for years, and fully exonerated in 2002 after Matias Reyes confessed and DNA matched him alone. R2: all are living public figures; use no faces, no portraits, no likenesses — silhouettes, hands, symbols only. The doc's subject is coerced juvenile confessions and wrongful conviction, framed as a justice documentary. Fully ad-safe. Do NOT sensationalize.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case (aggregates 2002 DA reinvestigation, Tejada vacatur order, 2014/2016 settlements)

ledger.claim: The victim (Trisha Meili) — clinical
ledger.detail: The victim of the assault was Patricia 'Trisha' Ellen Meili, a 28-year-old investment banker (a vice president at Salomon Brothers). She was for years known publicly only as 'the Central Park jogger' before disclosing her identity in a 2003 memoir. She is a living survivor. Treat with dignity; refer to her as 'the jogger' / 'Trisha Meili' plainly, no imagery of her, no graphic detail.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trisha_Meili — confirmed age 28, VP at Salomon Brothers, identity revealed April 2003 memoir 'I Am the Central Park Jogger'

ledger.claim: The attack — date and place (CLINICAL, non-graphic)
ledger.detail: On the night of April 19, 1989, Trisha Meili was attacked while jogging in Central Park, New York City, and was severely beaten and raped. STATE THIS CLINICALLY AND BRIEFLY — 'she was attacked and left for dead' is the ceiling of detail. No description of injuries, no re-enactment, no graphic language. This is a justice/false-confession documentary; the assault is context, not content.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case — confirmed April 19, 1989, ~9–10 p.m.

ledger.claim: Severity and survival (clinical)
ledger.detail: Meili was found hours later with severe injuries, lost a large volume of blood, and was in a coma for 12 days (regained consciousness May 1, 1989). She survived but had no memory of the attack itself. Keep clinical: 'she survived, but could not remember what happened.' The absence of her testimony is legally relevant because the case against the teens rested on their confessions, not on her account.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trisha_Meili — confirmed coma 12 days, no memory of the attack or hour before

ledger.claim: The five defendants — names and exact 1989 ages
ledger.detail: The five were juveniles when arrested in April 1989: Antron McCray (15), Kevin Richardson (14), Yusef Salaam (15), Raymond Santana (14), and Korey Wise (16; then known as 'Kharey' Wise). AGES ARE LOAD-BEARING — the whole injustice is that children were interrogated for hours and convicted on coerced confessions. State ages precisely.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case — ages confirmed exactly: McCray 15, Richardson 14, Salaam 15, Santana 14, Wise 16 (b. July 26 1972)

ledger.claim: The 'wilding' label (media term, contested origin)
ledger.detail: Police and press described a group of teens as 'wilding' in the park that night, and the word became a national headline. Its origin is DISPUTED: investigative reporter Barry Michael Cooper reported that officers misunderstood teens referencing 'doing the wild thing' (lyrics from Tone Loc's song 'Wild Thing'). Present 'wilding' as a MEDIA/POLICE label of the era, NOT as established fact about what the five did — attribute the term to the coverage, not to the boys.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case — origin attributed to Barry Michael Cooper / Tone Loc 'Wild Thing'; genuinely disputed
ledger.screen_phrasing: "The police and the papers called it 'wilding' — a word that became a national headline. Its origin is disputed; one account traces it to officers mishearing teenagers quoting a rap lyric. It described the media panic, not a proven act by these five."

ledger.claim: The arrests (night of April 19-20, 1989)
ledger.detail: Police detained a number of teenagers in and around Central Park that night in connection with several assaults reported in the park. The five were taken into custody and questioned over the following hours/days. They were rounded up amid a chaotic night of multiple reported incidents; the connection to the jogger attack was made by police during interrogation, not by physical evidence.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case

ledger.claim: The interrogations — hours, largely unrecorded, juveniles (THE CORE INJUSTICE)
ledger.detail: The teens were subjected to lengthy police interrogation. FIRM, VERIFIED: the videotaped statements began April 21 after the suspects had been in custody for AT LEAST SEVEN HOURS of unrecorded interrogation; only the final statements were taped. The larger cumulative-hours figures sometimes cited (e.g. into the low tens of hours across the group, '~30 hours') are REPORTED/APPROXIMATE and were NOT independently confirmed this pass. This is the heart of the false-confession problem: hours of unrecorded pressure, then a short taped statement.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case — 'in custody for at least seven hours' before videotaping confirmed; larger cumulative totals not verified
ledger.screen_phrasing: FIRM: "By the time the cameras were switched on, the boys had been in custody for at least seven hours — none of it recorded." If a larger total is used: "Some accounts describe interrogations stretching far longer — as much as a day or more across the group" (frame as reported, never as an exact figure).

ledger.claim: Absence of parents/counsel — especially Korey Wise
ledger.detail: Korey Wise, 16, gave his videotaped statement ALONE — without a parent, guardian, or attorney present. The three younger boys who were videotaped (Santana, McCray, Richardson) had a parent present for the taped statement, but the preceding unrecorded questioning is where the pressure was applied. Keep precise: FIRM that Wise had no parent/guardian/counsel for his statement; do NOT overstate that all five had no adult for all questioning.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case — Wise videotaped alone (no parent/counsel); Santana/McCray/Richardson videotaped with a parent present

ledger.claim: The confessions — coerced, taped/oral breakdown, later recanted
ledger.detail: VERIFIED breakdown: FOUR of the five gave videotaped statements — Raymond Santana, Antron McCray, and Kevin Richardson (each with a parent present) and Korey Wise (alone). Yusef Salaam gave an ORAL (untaped) statement only; his videotaped statement was not taken/was rejected after he requested counsel — he signed and taped nothing. All statements were extracted after hours of unrecorded interrogation and were quickly recanted. The five have consistently said the confessions were coerced — that they were fed details, told they could go home if they talked, and pressured as frightened children. FRAME AS COERCED/FALSE.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case — videotaped: Santana, McCray, Richardson, Wise; Salaam oral/untaped only

ledger.claim: The confessions contradicted each other and the crime scene
ledger.detail: The statements were mutually inconsistent and did not match the known facts — they disagreed on time, place, who did what, what the victim wore, and how the attack unfolded. No confession accurately described the crime scene. This internal contradiction is a hallmark of the 2002 reinvestigation's conclusion that the confessions were unreliable.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case (2002 Ryan affirmation summary)

ledger.claim: NO DNA match at trial — semen excluded all five
ledger.detail: The DNA/serology evidence available at the 1990 trials EXCLUDED all five defendants. Semen recovered from the victim and scene did not match any of the five; it belonged to an unidentified male. Prosecutors proceeded on the confessions despite the exculpatory forensic result. THIS IS LOAD-BEARING: the state convicted five children on coerced confessions while the physical evidence pointed to someone else. State it plainly.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case — no DNA/semen match to any of the five at trial

Trump did NOT name the teens, but the ad was universally understood as about this case. FRAME NEUTRALLY as documented public record of the media/political climate. The $85,000 is a reported estimate — hedge it.

ledger.claim: Media firestorm and race
ledger.detail: The case became a national symbol of urban crime and was covered with intense, racialized language. Five Black and Latino teenagers were tried in the press before trial. Race, class, and a fearful city are essential context for how coerced confessions went unquestioned. Handle soberly and factually; the theme is documented, not speculative.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case (contemporaneous coverage and retrospectives)

ledger.claim: First trial (1990) — McCray, Salaam, Santana
ledger.detail: The first trial ran approximately June 25 to August 18, 1990. Defendants: Antron McCray, Yusef Salaam, and Raymond Santana. All three were convicted. They were tried as juveniles.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case — first trial June 25–Aug 18, 1990 (McCray, Salaam, Santana)

ledger.claim: Second trial (1990) — Richardson and Wise; Wise tried as an ADULT
ledger.detail: The second trial ran from approximately October 22 to December 1990. Defendants: Kevin Richardson (14, tried as a juvenile) and Korey Wise (16). Because Wise was 16, he was CHARGED AND TRIED AS AN ADULT under New York law of the time — the pivotal fact that sent him to adult jails and made his years the longest and hardest. Both were convicted.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case — second trial Oct 22–Dec 1990 (Richardson, Wise); Wise the only one tried as an adult

ledger.claim: Charges and convictions (acquitted of the top count)
ledger.detail: The five were convicted of various felonies arising from that night — the convictions included rape, assault, and robbery (and related riot charges); they were ACQUITTED of the most serious count (attempted murder). The precise per-defendant verdict mix varies by defendant. Keep it accurate: convicted of serious felonies including rape and assault; acquitted of attempted murder. Do NOT recite an exact per-person charge list on screen.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case — convicted of assault/robbery/rape/riot charges; acquitted of attempted murder; per-defendant mix varies

ledger.claim: Sentences — juveniles 5-10 years; Wise 5-15 years as an adult
ledger.detail: The four tried as juveniles (McCray, Richardson, Salaam, Santana) received indeterminate juvenile sentences of roughly 5 to 10 years. Korey Wise, sentenced as an adult, received roughly 5 to 15 years and was sent to adult prison. State the two tiers clearly; the adult sentence for Wise is the reason his story is the emotional spine of the prison act.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case — 5–10 yrs juvenile (four); 5–15 yrs adult (Wise)

ledger.claim: Time actually served
ledger.detail: The four juveniles served roughly 6 to 7 years each (Santana released ~1995; McCray ~1996; Richardson and Salaam ~1997). Korey Wise served roughly 13 years and was not released until 2002, after Reyes confessed (some sources say ~14 years — hedge Wise's figure). State served-time as approximate.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_jogger_case & https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korey_Wise — four served ~6–7 yrs (released 1995–1997); Wise ~13 yrs (released 2002; his page says ~14)

ledger.claim: Korey Wise in the adult system
ledger.detail: Because he was tried as an adult, Wise served his sentence in the adult prison system — reportedly including Rikers Island early on and state facilities such as Attica and, later, Auburn (where he crossed paths with Reyes). He was the oldest, served the longest, and happened to be incarcerated near Matias Reyes, which set the exoneration in motion. Keep the prison detail sober and non-graphic. NOTE: the specific facility list (Rikers/Attica) is commonly reported but was not confirmed this pass — Auburn IS confirmed as the site of the Reyes encounter; hedge the rest.
ledger.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korey_Wise (adult system, exact facilities not enumerated) & https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matias_Reyes (Auburn Correctional Facility, ~2001)

ledger.claim: DNA match to Reyes — and he acted ALONE
ledger.detail: DNA testing in 2002 confirmed Matias Reyes as the source of the semen recovered from the victim (matched to a factor of one in 6,000,000,000). This is the forensic hinge of the exoneration: one man's DNA, no accomplices.

ledger.detail: By the time Reyes confessed in 2002, the statute of limitations for the jogger attack had expired, so he was not (and could not be) newly charged for it. He remained imprisoned for his other convictions. State plainly to preempt the natural viewer question 'why wasn't he charged?'

ledger.claim: The DA reinvestigation (Morgenthau / Nancy Ryan)
ledger.detail: Manhattan District Attorney Robert Morgenthau's office reinvestigated. ledger.claim: The justice theme — juvenile interrogation and false-confession science
ledger.detail: The case is a landmark in the study of false confessions, especially by juveniles: youths are disproportionately likely to confess falsely under prolonged, unrecorded interrogation, to accept suggested details, and to comply with authority to end the ordeal. The case contributed to reform pushes for recording interrogations and for protections when minors are questioned. Present the SCIENCE as established (well-documented research consensus), while attributing specific reforms carefully. This is the doc's thesis and its ad-safe 'why it matters' spine.
ledger.source: False-confession research literature (Kassin et al.); case retrospectives. Present as research consensus; attribute specific reforms carefully.
